name: Suvorexant
description: Suvorexant (Belsomra) facts: how this orexin-blocking sleep medicine works, dosing basics, risks, interactions, overdose, and legal access.
quick: Suvorexant (Belsomra) is a sleep medicine that blocks orexin, a brain chemical that keeps you awake, rather than boosting GABA like benzodiazepines and Z-drugs. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance, but studies show little withdrawal when it is stopped.

blocks.p: Suvorexant is approved for insomnia with difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.[[1]]

Orexins are brain chemicals that promote wakefulness. By blocking their receptors, suvorexant helps switch off wake signals. Similar medicines include lemborexant (Dayvigo) and daridorexant (Quviviq).

The figures below come from the FDA-approved label and describe how prescribers typically use suvorexant. They are not personal dosing advice. A prescriber sets the dose for each person and adjusts it over time.[[1]]
Take only with at least 7 hours left before waking. Taking it with or soon after a large meal delays its effect.

sections.q: What are the risks and side effects of suvorexant?

blocks.p: **Common side effects** include next-day drowsiness, headache, dizziness, and abnormal dreams.[[1]]

**Other risks** include next-day impairment of driving at 20 mg, sleep paralysis, hallucinations when falling asleep or waking, cataplexy-like muscle weakness, complex sleep behaviors, and worsening depression.[[1]]

sections.q: What does suvorexant overdose look like?

blocks.p: Experience with overdose is limited. High doses cause dose-related sleepiness. Combined with alcohol or other sedatives the effects are harder to predict.[[1]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, hard to wake, or breathing slowly.
For advice when the person is awake and stable, call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222 (US, free, 24 hours).
If opioids could be involved, including pills not from a pharmacy, give naloxone if you have it. Naloxone does not reverse suvorexant, but it will not harm the person.
Stay with the person and place them on their side if they are drowsy or vomiting.

blocks.p: In clinical trials, stopping suvorexant after up to a year of use did not cause withdrawal symptoms or significant rebound insomnia. It is Schedule IV because high doses produced drug-liking similar to zolpidem in people who misuse sedatives.[[1]]

timeline.title: Sleep may be lighter
timeline.text: Some people notice a return of their original insomnia.

sections.q: How do you get suvorexant legally in the US?

blocks.p: In the United States, suvorexant is a Schedule IV controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[[2]]

ul: **Refills:** a Schedule IV prescription can be refilled up to five times within six months of the date it was written. After that, a new prescription is needed.[[3]]

**Telehealth:** federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[[4]]
**Monitoring:** prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.

**Pharmacies:** a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[[5]][[6]]
**Cost:** suvorexant is brand-only and costs more than generic sleep medicines; insurers often require trying a generic first.

blocks.p: **Traveling:** keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

Yes, but only with a valid prescription and only from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Many licensed pharmacies, including mail-order pharmacies run by insurers, fill suvorexant prescriptions online and ship them. Buying suvorexant from a website that does not require a prescription is illegal, and the product is often fake.[[5]][[7]]

steps: A clinician evaluates you in person or by telemedicine and decides whether suvorexant is appropriate.
The prescription goes to a pharmacy
Prescriptions for controlled medicines are usually sent electronically, straight from the prescriber to the pharmacy you choose.
The pharmacy checks and fills it
A pharmacist verifies the prescription and your identity, then dispenses the medicine in person or by mail.

blocks.p: **Signs that an online seller is illegal:**

ul: It sells suvorexant with no prescription, or after only a short online questionnaire.
It takes orders through social media, messaging apps, or email.
It asks for payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or money transfers.
It has no US street address, no state pharmacy license, and no pharmacist to speak to.
Its prices are far below those of ordinary pharmacies, or it ships from another country.

blocks.p: The FDA's BeSafeRx tool links to each state's license lookup, and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy lists verified online pharmacies.[[5]][[6]]

sections.q: Is suvorexant legal in other countries?

blocks.p: Laws change and differ in detail. Check current rules before carrying any controlled medicine across a border.[[8]]

faq: How is Belsomra different from Ambien?
Belsomra blocks wake-promoting orexin signals, while Ambien enhances GABA. Belsomra has a lower risk of dependence and withdrawal.
It has a low risk of dependence, but it is Schedule IV because people who misuse sedatives liked high doses in studies.
People with narcolepsy should not take it, because it blocks the same system that is missing in narcolepsy.
